chapter: New Orleans bands, clubs and players
title: Red Garter band changes and George Lewis's group
summary: George Lewis takes over the Red Garter, with a modern-sounding earlier band, a weak pianist and a better-sounding room.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: Well, what about the other places on Bourbon Street, like the Red Garter?
Well, the Red Garter. Yeah, I heard the stuff there. I've been there when I went to the Sunday afternoon. And I was calling for girls to play. And now when yours, Lewis.
George Lewis has just taken the place of Jim Lipsman's band there.
Yeah, the Clannotella was fired from then. That's why the whole band left.
And I think they went to your father's mustache.
Yeah, right.
What did that band play like?
Well, it was kind of a modern Dixman band, I would say. Both Ervin Alcon and Fregassoll played more modern than they usually do.
Did they sound like Eddie Connan's band, or did they sound like Turk Martin?
Well, they didn't sound like any particular band. It's just more modern style in some way.
Dixieland?
Yeah, more Dixieland style in India. Alcon didn't change so much, but Fregassof was the one that changed more.
What about George Lewis's band there? Do they play the same as they played Preservation Hall?

Yeah, I would say so. But they don't have the same line-up. They have a different piano player and they don't have a bass. Actually, he sounds better with the white piano player. It's an old Yardhunt. Yeah, he plays better than all the others, I would say. But the others can't keep the right chords and the right beat all the time. None of the guys in the band likes Eddie Connan. I don't know why they play with that. Because they always ask me to sit in and they always say that she's bad all the time. And she don't like to play it either.
She seems soft to me. She doesn't like to play New Orleans music? No.

She wants to play modern stuff. She plays with her son. She has a band with her son, so they play more modern jazz. Her favorite music is Latin music. She told me. She said it's just like work nowadays. It's a drag to play it and it's too much hard work, she said. Playing this chord. She plays a lot of wrong chords also. Like when George plays Pagano Street Blues, she just leaves out two chords in it. It sounds very funny. George don't like it either because he's kind of blowing in her ear and trying to make it the right chord.
But at that other place they had Sim Zimmerman on piano, Dave Oxley, Jack Willis and Williamson.
It's another trumpet, yeah. I don't usually play with him. With the horn. Yeah. Yeah.
So that makes a difference in the sound.
Yeah, it's not too much different, but it's kind of better. It sounds better really. I think that might be because the sound of the hall is better there. The sound in the room is much better.
